build_phj: release with the multi-dimension PHJ (branch 55-join-probe, feat commit 45289da911)
build_ht: release original (main): multi-condition joins use the regular HT
notes: The PHJ side was re-measured on the committed multi-dimension PHJ source (feat commit 45289da911, 21 repeats); the HT side ran on the original main build (7 repeats, measured in the same session).

Every number at or below 3 ms sits at the 1 ms CLI timer resolution, so the small-workload ratios (2D 100^2, 2D 300^2, 3D 21^3, 3D 40^3) are noise-level and carry no conclusion. The 3D 90^3 and the probe workloads are above the floor and carry the findings.

The build-dominated 3D 90^3 self join loses: PHJ 20 ms against HT 16 ms (0.8x). The PHJ build scans D key columns and gathers into the position table, which is structurally more work than the vectorized hash build for a single pass.

The probe-dominated workload (1k build by 1M probe) shows a 1.33x PHJ gain in 3D (3 ms against 4 ms) and parity in 2D. The probe-side position table lookup is O(1), which is where the probe-dominated gain comes from; the advantage is small at this scale.
The PHJ is correct: the existing PHJ suite passes and the multi-dimension verification in benchmark/lattice/verify_phj.sh confirms the analytic counts and payload sums.
Follow-up: measure probe-dominated workloads at a larger probe scale and with a payload projection, where the probe-side output dominates.
